answer: In an agent economy spanning tundra monitoring, nebula mapping and falcon tracking, each voting identity must lock tokens for 30 days. Votes are weighted by locked tokens, so splitting 1,000 tokens among ten fake agents yields the same influence as one agent staking 1,000. Creating identities adds no voting power: an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, tying up capital and losing its use elsewhere during the lock.
